title: QUANTIFYING THE AESTHETIC FOR STREETSCAPES: APPLICATION OF DEEP LEARNING TO ASHIHARA’S AESTHETIC TOWNSCAPE
base_model: DeepLabv3+ (ResNet50 encoder, 'downscale' model); ResNet50 ADE20K segmentation model used as-is for buildings
target_classes: secondary profile (billboards, outdoor advertisements, signboards); primary profile (building outline; via ADE20K model, not retrained)
results: DeepLab V3+ downscale [trained on own annotated Tokyo street images (+augmentation)] mIoU=63.17% @ own 1,099 test images (secondary profiles) | Benchmark (ResNet50, ImageNet-pretrained encoder) [trained on smaller own set (439 train images), no augmentation] mIoU=23.74% @ own 147 test images (secondary profiles)
best_model_claim: DeepLab V3+ downscale model (more than double the benchmark accuracy)
label_efficiency_note: Benchmark trained on 439 images (val 148/test 147) reached 23.74% mIoU vs 63.17% with 3,736 training images plus data augmentation; authors attribute the gain to the larger dataset and augmentation.
evidence: Method (Data Collection, Selection of Deep Learning Model) and Table 1 (accuracy comparison, reproduced from Kumakoshi et al. 2021); split ratio 0.68:0.12:0.2; analysis set 5,459 GoPro street images of Ginza; primary profiles taken from ADE20K-trained ResNet50 model without retraining.

Railway front-view (train-mounted camera, 22 classes), private RTRI data; DL is the unmodified fine-tuned baseline, not a pre-adaptation baseline.
